stem: Determine the domain and range of $f(x) = {=b}^x{=signed(q)}$. Which of the following is correct?
solution: The power ${=b}^x$ can be calculated for every real number $x$, so there is no restriction on $x$: the domain is $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
Compare $f(x) = {=b}^x{=signed(q)}$ with $y = ab^x + q$: here $a = 1$, which is positive, and $q = {=q}$.
Because $a > 0$, the power ${=b}^x$ is positive for every $x$, so $f(x) = {=b}^x{=signed(q)}$ is always greater than ${=q}$: the graph lies above the line $y = {=q}$.
The graph gets closer and closer to $y = {=q}$ but never reaches it, so ${=q}$ is not part of the range. The range is $y \in ({=q}, \infty)$, with a round bracket.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Ignores q: takes y = 0 as the boundary of the range
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student states the range of y = ab^x + q as (0, infinity) or (-infinity, 0), forgetting that q moves the boundary line from y = 0 to y = q.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Puts the range on the wrong side of y = q
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student gives (-infinity, q) when a is positive, or (q, infinity) when a is negative, instead of using the sign of a to decide whether the graph lies above or below y = q.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Includes y = q in the range
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student writes a square bracket, [q, infinity) or (-infinity, q], as if the graph reached the line y = q. It only gets closer and closer, so the bracket must be round.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Swaps domain and range
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student restricts x by the boundary value q and says every real number is an output, the wrong way round: for an exponential the domain is all real numbers and the range is restricted.

notes: Basic entry point, modelled on the book's y = 2^x range with a vertical shift q added. a is fixed at 1 so the family has one skeleton (range above y = q); the opposite direction is practised in the standard and advanced families and appears here as a distractor. q is never 0 so that the 'range from zero' and 'swapped' options stay distinct from the key. mcq because the answer is an interval with infinity: every distractor is a named error. The domain is always R for y = ab^x + q.
